title: Lesson 5: No More Borrowing! - Vedic Subtraction
subtopics: Convert and add - the borrow-free method
learningGoals: Apply All From 9, Last From 10 to convert and then add - eliminating borrowing from all subtractions.
Solve 3-digit and 4-digit subtraction problems in money and measurement contexts without borrowing.
Build speed and confidence by eliminating the mental burden of regrouping entirely.
coreIdeas: Any subtraction can be converted to an addition using the complement - no borrowing ever needed.
Find the complement of the number being subtracted, then add it to the starting number.
The method works equally well for money (rupees/paise), length (cm), and weight (g) problems.

workedExamples.question: Rs 500 - Rs 237 = ?
workedExamples.method: Complement of 237 from 1000: 763. Add 500+763=1263, subtract 1000: Rs 263.

onboarding.coachIntro: Today you will turn subtraction into a calmer job by using complements first, so borrowing does not boss you around.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at group A. If the learner already knows complements fluently, jump to group C.

mission.missionPromise: Refresh complements first, then use them to solve subtraction without the usual borrowing struggle.
mission.successCelebration: Borrowing-free forever! You can subtract any number using complements and addition!

microLessonPattern: Coach shows the complement of the subtracted number.
Board demonstrates converting subtraction to an addition.
Student finds the complement first, then adds, then adjusts.
Instant feedback highlights which complement digit was wrong.
Review prompt asks the student to explain why borrowing is not needed.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 18 XP per exercise group based on difficulty.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Keep the streak counter visible; a correct answer on retry still counts as streak-save.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group earns a themed badge tied to the borrow-free skill being practised.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Short coach cheer, XP pulse animation, and progress bar moves forward.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two wrong answers in one group triggers a mini re-teach with a simpler number.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Re-show the complement derivation, then give a simpler number to try.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after the student answers the checkpoint correctly.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Missed groups reappear at the start of the next session as warm-up cards.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise B: Convert subtraction to addition
sessionFlow.coachHook: Here is the big idea: instead of subtracting, find the complement of what you are subtracting, then ADD it to your starting number!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: 237 - 89: complement of 89 from 100 = 11. 237+11=248. But we added 100 extra, so subtract 100: 248-100=148.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Borrow-free! Convert, add, adjust - you never touched borrowing once.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Real life! Let's use our borrow-free method to solve money problems - the kind you face at the market every day!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Rani has Rs 500. She spends Rs 237 on books. How much is left? Complement of 237=763. 500+763=1263. 1263-1000=Rs 263.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Rani has Rs 500 and spends Rs 237. How much remains?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Mohan has Rs 1000. He buys a bat for Rs 468. How much is left?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: A shopkeeper has Rs 750. He pays Rs 283 for stock. What remains?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant real-life maths! No borrowing in the market either.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: For Rs 1000-Rs 468: complement of 468=532. Answer: Rs 532.
